title: What contemplation is
hookLine: a gaze of faith fixed on Jesus, being with God rather than thinking about him (CCC 2715)
carry: I look at him, he looks at me

lines: WHAT DO YOU DO ALL THAT TIME?
cards: Every day, an old farmer would stop in the village church and sit there a long time. Not moving his lips, not reading, not holding beads. Just sitting, looking toward the tabernacle.
People noticed. This was Ars, a little French village in the 1800s, and the parish priest was John Vianney, now a saint.
He finally asked the farmer what he did all that time, and the answer was so simple that the Catholic Church put it in its Catechism. Today's word is what he was doing.

teach.h: I LOOK AT HIM, HE LOOKS AT ME.
teach.b: First, the farmer's answer. As the story is told, he said: I look at him, and he looks at me. No technique.
No words. Two people looking at each other. The Catechism calls contemplation a gaze of faith fixed on Jesus, and tells this story to explain it.
Second, the word itself. Contemplation comes from Latin, and inside it is templum, the same root as temple.

teach.h: TEMPLUM: A SPACE MARKED OUT TO WATCH.
teach.b: A templum was a patch of sky or ground marked out by Roman priests for watching carefully. To contemplate was to mark out a space and look, with full attention. Catholics took the word and pointed it at God.
Third, how it's different. Catholics describe three expressions of prayer.

Vocal prayer uses words: the Our Father, the rosary. Meditation uses the mind: you think about a Gospel scene and turn it over. Contemplation is simpler: being with God rather than thinking about him.
Saint Teresa of Avila, a Spanish nun of the 1500s, described it as time spent alone with the one we know loves us, like close friends. With a close friend, you don't need to talk the whole time.
Fourth, a psalm from camp four says it in one line. In the Douay-Rheims: "Be still and see that I am God."
The Church teaches that contemplation isn't just for monks and nuns.

teach.h: BE STILL AND SEE THAT I AM GOD.
teach.b: It's a gift God can give anyone, in a kitchen or a car or a pew. The farmer from Ars had no degree and no method. He just showed up, and looked.

how: Many Catholics practice silent prayer before the Blessed Sacrament in Eucharistic adoration, sitting in a church or chapel simply to be with Christ, often for an hour at a time.

o: thinking hard about a Bible passage
a quiet gaze of faith, being with God
saying many prayers out loud in a row

games.q: what's inside the word — tap the pairs.
p: I look at him, he looks at me
a space marked out for watching

s: contemplation is only for monks and nuns
the Church teaches it's a gift God can give anyone, like the old farmer at Ars.
contemplation shares a root with the word temple
both come from Latin templum, a space marked out for watching.
contemplation means thinking hard about God
that's closer to meditation. contemplation is a gaze: being with God rather than thinking about him.

games.q: you're the parish priest of Ars. an old farmer sits in church for an hour a day, lips still, no book. you ask him what he does. what does he say?
o: I say all my prayers from memory.
I look at him, and he looks at me.
I rest my legs after the fields.
games.why: as the story is told: I look at him, and he looks at me. the Catechism uses it to explain contemplation.

practice: Place a crucifix or an icon in front of you for a minute or longer, or if you don't have one, a picture on your phone, a candle, or simply the sky through a window.
Don't try to think anything about it; just look, and when your mind wanders, and it will, come back to looking.
If you pray, you can let yourself be looked at in return, the way the farmer did; if you don't, just rest in seeing one thing fully.

wordCard.voice: Contemplation. A gaze of faith: being with God rather than thinking about him. Today's word.

orig.note: Latin: contemplation, from templum, a space marked out for watching.

carryVoice: Your line: I look at him, he looks at me. No words needed. That's day two hundred thirty-two.
